title: Machines and computation histories

based_on.title: Computability and Incompleteness
based_on.pages: 35–41 (§2.6, machine equivalence, primitive-recursive histories and search; version 2007-01-09)

based_on.title: Formalizing Computability Theory via Partial Recursive Functions
based_on.pages: 12:9–12:13 (§§4.2–5.2, paired recursive programs and resource-bounded evaluation; ITP 2019)

summary: Record a computation as numbered states, check its finite history, and prove that one search for such a history computes every partial recursive function.
abstract: A machine that halts leaves a finite record of its successive states. Checking that record can be much simpler than knowing in advance whether the machine will stop. We define an arithmetic machine whose state is a number and whose transitions are primitive-recursive calculations, and prove that its successful runs have primitive-recursive certificate tests. These machines compute exactly the partial recursive functions: searching for a certified history computes a machine's output, while evaluation with increasing finite resource allowances supplies a machine for every recursive program. Even a program containing nested searches can therefore be expressed using one unbounded search for a finite certificate, followed by extraction of its output.
